problems.source_says: Figure 3a displays a corpus of 31 stories entering evaluation, but the paper does not establish that 31 is the number of observations in the writing quality analysis. The analysis unit, aggregation across raters, and outcome-specific analysis sample are unspecified. The form itself leaves unit null and acknowledges that the figure count is not a stated number of statistical observations. Under codebook sections 6 and 7, n_units counts observations in the paper's analysis; retain the figure label in notes and set n_units to null.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2, S1-O3 and S1-O4 are expert blind evaluations of participants' written work, covering writing quality, content quality and originality. These support expert_raters, scored_on_output=true, usefulness for the quality dimensions and novelty for originality.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Fig. 2a and caption; codebook section 6, Construct and Measure.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 accurately transcribes output quality improving by 18%, t = 3.18, p < 0.01, df = 68. The quality label supports usefulness; the experiment uses expert review, although the summary formula and its relation to the three dimensions are unspecified, as the form notes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Productivity effects of generative AI, second paragraph; p. 9, Fig. 2 caption. Supplementary Figure 10 is cited but absent from the saved PDF.

confirmed.statement: S1 has ChatGPT assistance during writing, supporting ai_available_when_produced=yes and with_ai. Fig. 2a places tool sign-up between Task 1 and Task 2; the initial task is before AI access, not an unassisted task after AI removal.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Fig. 2a and caption; p. 10, Productivity effects of generative AI; codebook section 1.

confirmed.statement: S2-O3, S2-O4 and S2-O5 concern experts' evaluations of the participants' adventure stories for writing quality, content quality and originality. They are output ratings, not self-reports; usefulness and novelty are the appropriate construct mappings.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Fig. 3 caption, Phase 2 description; codebook section 6.

confirmed.statement: S2-O1 accurately records the individual-creativity increases: one AI idea, 42.1%, t = 5.30, p < 0.01, df = 149; five AI ideas, 16.4%, t = 2.52, p < 0.05, df = 149. The individual-creativity label supports overall_creativity, while the exact score formula is not supplied.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI, first paragraph; p. 11, Fig. 3 caption describes expert story evaluation. Supplementary Figures 21-22 are cited but absent.

confirmed.statement: S2-O2 exactly preserves the reported collective-diversity decrease of 5.64%-6.47% and the unusual printed tests t = 5.52; t = 54.80, p < 0.05, df = 28. The paragraph does not map those numbers to particular arms or languages, so the form correctly avoids that allocation.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI, first paragraph, baseline-replication sentence.

confirmed.statement: S2 participants wrote their stories under zero, one or five AI suggestions, before expert evaluation. Thus the rated-story outcomes are with_ai, while collective convergence of different writers' stories is diversity/across_people, not within-person flexibility or after_ai.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Human creativity and generative AI; p. 11, Fig. 3a and caption; p. 12, first paragraph; codebook sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: The saved paper does not specify the statistical observation units or rater aggregation for these outcomes. Leaving unit null is warranted; neither the test degrees of freedom nor the diagram's story count establishes an analysis unit.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 9-12, Figs. 2-3 and the two writing-study result sections; codebook section 6, Unit.

confirmed.statement: S2-O2 correctly leaves measure null: the paper reports convergence of outputs but supplies no operational diversity metric, embedding model, pairing rule or aggregation formula.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 10-12, Human creativity and generative AI and Fig. 3 caption.

confirmed.statement: No additional qualifying outcome was identified in the complete saved document. S1 completion time, self-efficacy, enjoyment and AI attitudes do not score output creativity/diversity; S3 concerns ethical judgments, sentiment and leniency. Fig. 3b places DAT questions before the AI-writing intervention.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Productivity effects of generative AI; p. 11, Fig. 3b; pp. 12-14, Moral reasoning in human-AI interactions and Fig. 4. Entire markdown read through its final reference.

confirmed.statement: The 25-page saved PDF ends with references and has no appended or embedded Supplementary Information. Both attempts to access named supplementary-source leads were blocked by the environment with WinError 10013, leaving the missing analysis details unverified.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 18, Data, Materials, Software Availability; p. 25, final references; PDF embedded-file inventory. Failed urllib requests: https://api.github.com/repos/epitome-AISS/epitome/contents/ and https://www.epitome-ai.com/.

summary: The form records n_units=31 for S2-O3, S2-O4 and S2-O5 without establishing that the figure's story count is the number of analysis observations. Criterion 3 holds because experts explicitly evaluated participants' written outputs, including originality.
